scope: Main 100D normal-CDF-skewed t(3) comparison at the recorded revision
excluded: This is not a fresh audit of the other six production experiments.
conclusion: The inspected code supports a reproducible, specified-budget comparison of radial estimation conditional on fitted maps. No accidental extra SCS pretuning was found in the current call path. Equal tuning resources do not establish equally effective or optimal tuning; boundary v2 contains an explicit reflected-only step constraint. These results alone do not establish full-distribution mixing or a universal method ranking.

upstream_provenance.verification: All three local Git blob identities match the pinned upstream Git tree; published source inventory of 207 files matched the reviewed revision.

corrected_execution_issue.before: A partial wave (18 remaining chains with 32 workers) could occupy different subsets of pinned workers for different methods.
corrected_execution_issue.after: Close the larger pool before initializing a pool of exactly the partial-wave size. Every method occupies the same ordered CPU prefix. Check completed allocations and record expected/actual CPU assignments. Affinity is established before JAX import.
corrected_execution_issue.qualification: Windows/Linux pin CPU affinity; macOS explicitly records OS-managed allocation. Hardware load, temperature, scheduling and timed stopping still affect measurements.
corrected_execution_issue.rerun: Rerun every compared method together for corrected timings, especially runs with partial worker waves.

matched_components.finding: All current methods evaluate the same canonical normal-CDF-skewed t(3) target. Radial truths are analytic, avoiding simulated-reference error. This is not the SCS paper's Student-t-CDF target.

Both map families use the same fit_map call, update and draw budgets, fresh batches, Adam settings, gradient norm cap, and zero/unit parameter convention. Both BW variants share the fitted ball map. The legacy author VI routine is not called by the current runner.

The current driver uses the same observed-acceptance dual averaging and warmup iteration budget for all methods, with the documented reflected-only ceiling exception. Maps and final steps are frozen for timed sampling; warmup and production use separate PRNG splits. Every method starts warmup at physical ones.

Empirical MSE averages per-chain squared errors. Every post-burn iteration contributes, including rejection repeats; thinning affects stored traces only. Paired error differences align methods by unique saved seed IDs. Empirical uncertainty is labelled descriptive and conditional on fitted maps.

reflection_math.conclusion: No missing Hastings ratio found. Valid in exact arithmetic with a fixed proposal scale.
reflection_math.reason: Condition on an unoriented line. The signed radial step has even density g(s)=d*abs(s)^(d-1)/(2*h^d) on [-h,h]. Folding to [0,L] gives Q(z,zprime)=sum_k[g(zprime-z+2*k*L)+g(zprime+z+2*k*L)], symmetric in z,zprime. Ball volume disintegrates as dq dt; average the reversible line kernels over directions, then apply the transformed-target MH ratio.
reflection_math.floating_point_qualification: Invalid reflected endpoints self-loop without clipping; this is not a proof of exact reversibility on the floating-point grid.

independent_jacobian_and_initialization_.method: JAX autodifferentiation of the production physical projection; log(abs(det(J))) for the ball and restriction of the sphere Jacobian to an independently computed orthonormal tangent basis. Compare with transformed log density minus physical target log density.
independent_jacobian_and_initialization_.map_source: validation/scs_geometry_fits.json; archived fitted maps from optimized-jax-scs-100d-check

independent_scs_first_return_and_reverse.method: Draw unit-sphere points and uniform tangent directions, retain bright points, draw angular steps uniformly on [.001,pi/2-1e-5], retain cap crossings, compare author step-out to independently iterated geodesic rotations until first bright return. Reverse the final tangent and apply the same angular step and first-return rule.
independent_scs_first_return_and_reverse.rng_note: Continues after random directions used in the Jacobian check.

reproduction.scope: Checks geometry and constructed numerical edge cases; does not measure performance.

limitations.classification: Scope limitation, not an identified estimator bug
limitations.finding: Current 100D output retains norms and radial tail indicators, not physical directions. The radial law is unchanged by this target's skewing. Incorrect directional exploration could therefore be invisible to both reported metrics.
limitations.consequence: Restrict claims to the two radial functionals. A bounded projection statistic would strengthen any claim about sampling the skewed distribution; no expensive full diagnostic suite is required for that check.

limitations.finding: Boundary v2 leaves ordinary BW and SCS on the original log-scale ceiling of 15 and limits only reflected BW to step 2. The bound was selected after a pilot exposed unattainable acceptance-target calibration. It is not a demonstrated optimum and is not imposed on the controls.
limitations.consequence: Compare the specified procedures, not a pure boundary-only intervention. Preserve the pilot history and do not present historical common-cap v1 results as current v2 results. The documentation already makes this distinction.

limitations.finding: Acceptance-target adaptation optimizes neither reported MSE nor a common physical movement scale. Initial numeric scale 0.1 and target 0.234 have different implications for the proposal families. In both saved optimized main checks, SCS warmup-average acceptance was about 0.231 while production acceptance was about 0.181. This is not proof of an implementation error; warmup-average acceptance does not validate the final frozen scale.
limitations.consequence: Do not call the procedures equally optimally tuned. Strong claims of well-tuned performance would require predeclared sensitivity checks for every method using fresh evaluation randomness, not selective tuning to seek a desired ranking.

limitations.classification: Conditional benchmark design, not an identified one-sided fitting rule
limitations.finding: Same fitting budgets and parameter conventions do not imply identical induced initial distributions, optimization difficulty or achieved fit quality. Map families and fixed shape parameters differ. The implementation uses the final fixed-budget iterate without held-out fit certification or restarts. Raw objective histories omit family-specific constant base-density normalizations and should not be compared as absolute KL values across families.
limitations.consequence: Describe equal optimizer resources and recorded fits; do not claim equal fit quality or optimal maps. Multiple prespecified fit seeds would be needed to assess the entire fitting-and-sampling procedure rather than a single fit.

limitations.finding: Seed batches change sampling and warmup streams but hold default fit seed 42 fixed. Repeating a batch reuses the random streams; timed endpoints may differ without constituting an independent replication. Batch 0 has already appeared in exploratory checks. Different seed IDs do not by themselves validate a performance ranking.
limitations.consequence: Use fresh prespecified batches for evaluation and retain all outcomes. Treat uncertainty as conditional on the recorded map and timing regime. Do not count repeated batch-0 runs as independent evidence or choose which seeds to report by the winner.

limitations.finding: For t(3), radial density decays as r^-4: the second radial moment is finite but the fourth is infinite. Even an iid finite-length norm average can have an infinite fourth central moment, so the variance of its squared error need not exist. Empirical MSE MCSE and bootstrap ranges may miss rare extreme errors. The bounded tail indicator avoids this particular infinite-moment issue.
limitations.consequence: Retain the descriptive labels and influential-chain shares. Do not interpret them as formal confidence intervals or certify a ranking from one short run. More chains improve empirical coverage but do not prove stationarity or cure inadequate exploration.

timing_scope: Equal per-chain production time includes first-third burn-in, transitions and all-state radial accumulation. It excludes VI, compilation, separate step calibration, inter-worker waits and file/plot generation; separate costs are reported. This is not an equal-total-cost comparison.
author_code_scope: The unmodified pinned SCS transition is used with the shared external fitting/calibration on the DCS normal-CDF t(3) target. This does not reproduce the SCS paper target or complete published experiment.

upstream_numerical_edge_case.finding: Confirmed numerical edge case in unchanged upstream SCS, not a demonstrated problem in current benchmark runs.
upstream_numerical_edge_case.description: A constructed cap crossing with true angle about 2.01e-10 rounds dot(x,y) to one; arccos gives zero and the upstream step-out can return NaNs. Current finite-summary validation aborts such runs.
upstream_numerical_edge_case.impact: No demonstrated effect on the reported runs or rankings; no invalid endpoints in the 958 ordinary random cap-crossing checks. The vendored author code remains unchanged.

documentation_corrections: Distinguish historical fixed-step/original-VI SCS recipe from current shared calibration
Correct diagnostic coverage: current 100D comparisons have radial reports, not full ESS/R-hat/directional diagnostics
Explain radial-only inference, conditional fits, reflected-only bound and omitted family-specific constants in VI losses

execution_validation.local_partial_wave_smoke: Passed: three chains per method, two workers, seed batch 1, waves 2+1; report regeneration passed. macOS allocation is OS-managed.
execution_validation.interpretation: Execution verification only; no performance ranking is inferred from a quick check.
execution_validation.cross_platform_check: CI runs the same three-chain boundary smoke on Linux and Windows; per-commit outcomes are visible in GitHub Actions.
execution_validation.ci_legacy_pilot_adjustment: The historical joint-radius quick CI check explicitly uses 1.0 second for every pilot of both methods; production preset defaults remain unchanged. This repairs the earlier Windows smoke failure with fewer than four collected draws at 0.1 seconds.

reviewer_safe_claim: On the specified 100-dimensional normal-CDF-skewed t(3) target, we compare the recorded implementations at equal production-time budgets with common VI and warmup iteration budgets, using the same physical initialization and first-third burn-in. Results quantify empirical error for radial tail probability and mean norm, conditional on the fitted maps. The separate reflected-BW experiment uses a disclosed step ceiling of 2 selected after an exploratory pilot; ordinary BW and author SCS retain their original benchmark calibration. We do not infer optimal tuning, general mixing superiority, or a universal ranking from these results.
revision_note: Historical audit of the main comparison and boundary v2. Boundary v3 replaces the reflected-only bound of 2 with ball_esjd_pilot_v1; see docs/BOUNDARY_100D.md and validation/boundary_v3_checks.json. This file preserves the earlier findings and does not certify the new calibration.
